key_insight: DMRG finds a strong MPS starting point, and stopping MPS encoding at the logistic inflection point before using PITE avoids the deepest and least efficient part of state preparation.
engineering_relevance: This hybrid workflow reduces circuit depth and post-selection cost, making ground-state initialization more practical for near-term quantum simulation pipelines.
method: Use DMRG to compute an N-site ground-state MPS and estimate overlap/gap parameters.
Encode the MPS onto qubits with an optimization-free matrix-product disentangler (MPD) circuit up to the inflection layer L*.
Apply deterministically scheduled probabilistic imaginary-time evolution (PITE) to remove remaining excited-state error.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on the spin-1/2 staggered-field Heisenberg chain show that the approach avoids very deep encoding circuits and significantly lowers the post-selection overhead of PITE.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate classical preprocessing from DMRG and on problem-specific estimates of the gap and overlap, so performance may degrade when those quantities are hard to obtain or the target state is not well approximated by a low-bond-dimension MPS.
paper_title: Overcoming the Matrix-Product-State Encoding Barrier via DMRG-Guided Probabilistic Imaginary-Time Evolution
